title: FastVGGT: Fast Visual Geometry Transformer
claim: Quadratic full-token attention is slow and error-prone on long inputs; merging tokens makes it far faster and more accurate.
layout: Left: stacked ours-vs-baseline schematics; right: bar chart above two reconstructions; VS arrow
description: The figure has two halves. On the left, a dashed box compares two attention schemes. The top shows Fast-VGGT with complexity O((N/r)^2·d) as three rounded panels: Merge, Self-Attn and Unmerge. Green source and destination tokens are shown, and a rocket icon marks speed. Below it, after a red 'VS' banner, is VGGT with complexity O(N^2·d). It shows a large grid of green outlined tokens, and a snail icon marks slowness. A legend at the top defines raw, source and destination tokens. On the right, the title reads 'Single forward with 1000 images (4× speedup)'. A stacked bar chart of inference time against frame count compares VGGT, VGGT* and FastVGGT. An orange curve rises steeply, and a 'VGGT OOM' tag appears. Below the chart are two point-cloud reconstructions with Chamfer distance 0.27 for ours and 0.71 for VGGT.
caption: We propose FastVGGT, a training-free framework that processes 1,000 images in a single inference, achieving 4× faster while mitigating error accumulation. VGGT* refers to VRAMEfficient of VGGT, enabling larger inputs.
abstract: Scaling visual geometry transformers for long image sequences poses a significant computational and memory challenge. In this work, we diagnose this issue in the state-of-the-art model VGGT, and trace the primary bottleneck to its Global Attention layer. Our analysis reveals a ``token collapse'' phenomenon, where many tokens attend to nearly identical regions, resulting in redundant computation and inefficiency. Motivated by this finding, we propose FastVGGT, a training-free framework that strategically prunes these redundant tokens. Instead of uniform merging, FastVGGT employs a tailored, three-part token partitioning strategy. It preserves initial-frame tokens as a stable global reference, retains salient tokens to maintain fine details, and utilizes region-based random sampling to ensure spatially balanced coverage. Extensive experiments on multiple 3D geometry benchmarks validate our approach's effectiveness. Notably, on sequences of 1000 images, FastVGGT achieves a 4$\times$ speedup over the original VGGT while simultaneously mitigating error accumulation, demonstrating its efficiency and robustness for long-sequence scenarios. For further details, please visit our project page: https://mystorm16.github.io/fastvggt/.
